papers.title_in_file: Biclustering a dataset using photonic quantum computing
papers.what_it_is: A preprint proposing boson sampling and Gaussian boson sampling heuristics for biclustering, tested in four noiseless simulations on 12 x 12 synthetic datasets.

existing.note: The GBS comparison is stated against the authors' own current boson sampling encoding only, and Section 7 says the gap may come from that encoding rather than the hardware model. Both results come from four synthetic 12 x 12 noiseless simulations.
existing.value: The authors report that both boson sampling and GBS perform better when the contrast between the values inside and outside the bicluster is large, and that the GBS approach seems to produce comparable or better results for fewer samples, against their current way of performing boson sampling.
existing.anchor: Section 6.5 items 2 and 3, p.26; Section 7 item 1, p.27
quotes: Both boson sampling and GBS perform better when the contrast between the values that are inside and outside the bicluster is large.
The GBS approach seems to produce comparable or better results for fewer number of samples (against our current way of performing boson sampling).
the difference may be more to do with how we encode the problems for boson sampling.
existing.certainty_reason: Started LOW: an empirical result from one study.

existing.note: Stated in Section 6.5 item 5. It rests on one problem with three 4 x 4 biclusters in a 12 x 12 dataset (Section 6.4).

assertions.value: The authors state that their work is the first that attempts to apply boson sampling and GBS to the biclustering problem.
quotes: our work is the first that attempts to apply boson sampling and GBS to this problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they worked with a dataset of size 12 x 12 and biclusters of sizes 4 x 4 and 6 x 6, and that their aim was preliminary insight into the relation between photonic quantum computing and biclustering.
quotes: our primary aim is to gain preliminary insights about the relationship between photonic quantum computing and biclustering.
For this, we worked with dataset of size 12 × 12 and biclusters of sizes 4 × 4 and 6 × 6.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Section 3.

assertions.value: The authors state that all simulations were run on classical computers, used Perceval for boson sampling and Strawberry Fields for GBS, and were noiseless.
quotes: The programs were written in the Python programming language and the simulation packages used were Perceval for boson sampling and Strawberry Fields for GBS.
All our simulations were noiseless.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Section 6.

assertions.value: The authors state that they took four problems, two for boson sampling and two for GBS, on 12 x 12 datasets, and that their simulations were based on a simplified version of the proposed heuristics in algorithms 1 and 3.
quotes: We took a total of four problems : two for boson sampling and two for GBS with 12 × 12 sized datasets.
Another thing to note is that our simulations were based on a simplified version of the proposed heuristics in algorithms 1 and 3.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Section 6.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in boson sampling problem 1 with postselection at tau equal to 1, the success probability fell from 0.89 for the first dataset to 0.087 for the fifth dataset as the values outside the bicluster rose.
quotes: For example, for the data of postselect τ = 1, we can see how the results degrade when going from 0.89 for D(1) to 0.087 for D(5).
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors read this as the technique doing better when the bicluster differs enough in magnitude from the rest of the dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that the strictest postselection left only hundreds of samples out of the million taken, and state that meaningful postselection appears to need a very large number of samples.
quotes: After applying our strictest postselection criteria (postselect τ = 1 column), the samples that remain are only in the hundreds.
it would appear that in order to even conduct meaningful postselection, we need a very large number of samples.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the binary dataset with a bicluster of all ones and zeros elsewhere, the postselected success probability was observed to be 1, and state that a realistic binary dataset may not give so high a probability.
quotes: Here we can see that the postselected P is observed to be 1.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the traditional way to run boson sampling, with one photon per input mode and at most one photon per output mode, may not be best suited for practical applications and will face noise issues on a real photonic device.
quotes: may not be best suited for practical applications.
this stringent approach will face issues with noise once we would try and implement it on an actual photonic device [10]
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the second boson sampling problem the success probability of finding the square bicluster rose with the number of simulated annealing steps p, from 0.17 at 20 steps to 0.99 at 200 steps, over a hundred trials per p.
quotes: We ran our simulations for p steps that span over the entire annealing schedule T for p ∈ {20, 50, 100, 150, 200} for a hundred trials per p (500 total).

assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Table 2 gives 0.17 for 20 steps and 0.99 for 200 steps.

assertions.value: The authors state that the second boson sampling problem results rest on one problem only, so a more thorough study is warranted, and that the number of samples needed was one of the most glaring challenges.
quotes: Of course, since we have just considered one problem over here, a more thorough study in the future is warranted.
One of the most glaring challenges is the number of samples that we had to do for this process to work.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the success probability of random sampling for the 6 x 6 bicluster is about 7.43 x 10 to the minus 6, which is lower than the GBS success probabilities, and that the correct samples were in the majority except for the real-valued dataset at 1 mean photon per mode.
quotes: the best solution (assuming there is only one) becomes 1/134596 ≈ 7.43 × 10−6.
except in one case (real valued dataset, n per mode = 1), the correct samples were in the majority (i.e. the statistical mode).
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that GBS, like boson sampling, seems more effective at finding binary biclusters, and that the best number of mean photons per mode could differ from problem to problem.

assertions.value: The authors state that even the real-valued GBS results are orders of magnitude better than random sampling, and that the worst GBS results suggest probabilities of the order of 10 to the minus 4 against 10 to the minus 6 for random sampling.

assertions.value: The authors report that after the two most observed biclusters were removed, the chance of observing the remaining bicluster rose significantly, with the largest rise for the binary dataset.
quotes: Here, we see a significant increase of observing the remaining bicluster, with the largest rise seen for the binary dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the standard GBS process is a fixed circuit that runs in constant time for a given size, unlike a gate model algorithm or quantum annealing, so taking more samples is to an extent more tolerable.
quotes: circuit that runs in constant time (for a given size), unlike a gate-model quantum
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the major restriction of GBS here is that the subgraphs or biclusters it finds have an even numbered dimension, so odd sizes and specific b1 x b2 shapes need post-processing.
quotes: The major restriction is that the sub-graphs (or biclusters) that GBS finds will have a even numbered dimension (N is even).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit, Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors state that they only deal with non-overlapping biclusters, and that overlapping biclusters would need a more refined approach with a larger number of samples.
quotes: 19 In this work, we only deal with non-overlapping biclusters.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, footnote 19.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is quite possible that classical methods can outperform a direct application of boson sampling or GBS in the short term, and recommend comparison with classical methods and hybrid quantum-classical techniques as future work.
quotes: It is quite possible that classical methods can outperform a direct application of restricted models of quantum computing (like boson sampling and GBS),
Of course, further studies and a thorough comparison with classical methods is needed to make stronger claims.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: No classical baseline was run in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that they found boson sampling and GBS to be best suited for binary datasets and datasets with very high value contrast, and that direct GBS needs fewer samples and locates rows and columns simultaneously.
quotes: We found that these models are best suited for binary datasets and datasets where the contrast in the values is very high.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result or author claim from one study.
